dhpak1.1:0.3: Reverence to him, the Fortunate One, the Arahat, the Perfect Sambuddha
dhpak1.1:1.1: The world {1.1} [28.145] is shrouded in the great delusion of darkness, seeing to the end of the world,
dhpak1.1:1.2: he lighted up the True Dhamma, blazing forth with his psychic power.
dhpak1.1:2.1: After revering the feet of the illustrious Sambuddha,
dhpak1.1:2.2: and worshipping the True Dhamma, I pay respects to the Saṅgha.
dhpak1.1:3.1: Moved by compassion here and there, skilled in Dhamma and adhamma,
dhpak1.1:3.2: come to the true state of Dhamma, the Teacher (taught) lovely Dhamma Verses.
dhpak1.1:4.1: He taught with the impulse of compassion, with a very determined mind,
dhpak1.1:4.2: surely increasing the joy and gladness of Devas and of men.
dhpak1.1:5.1: Nurtured by the lineage, there is a subtle commentary on the meaning,
dhpak1.1:5.2: in the Tambapaṇṇi island, written in the island’s language.
dhpak1.1:6.1: But it is not successful for the welfare of other beings.
dhpak1.1:6.2: It is well to make it succeed for the welfare of the whole world.
dhpak1.1:7.1: Such was the hope of the virtuous
dhpak1.1:7.2: Elder Kumārakassapa, who is trained, and of steady mind. {1.2}
dhpak1.1:8.1: He respectfully made a request desiring that the True Dhamma should endure;
dhpak1.1:8.2: therefore the diffuse language and the way of the words
dhpak1.1:9.1: I put aside, and translating into the language of the texts, which is pleasing;
dhpak1.1:9.2: and whatever in the verses is not explained in the letter or in the words,
dhpak1.1:10.1: having explained everything, all according to its purpose,
dhpak1.1:10.2: I will speak a different language, bringing to those who have wisdom
dhpak1.1:10.3: joy and gladness in their minds, depending on practice and theory.
